- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early.
- Underestimate prices in the medium term (5-10 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; model fails to capture downward bias.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative (e.g., -2.49 or below), reduce forecast by 5-10% to avoid overconfidence in rebound.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1-2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: if sentiment is positive but forecast is lagging, add 0.5-1.5% per day to catch momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; smooth out forecast by averaging last 3 sentiment values before adjusting.
- For long-term (15+ days) forecasts, reduce forecast by 1-2% per day if sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down.
